text:
Blake Coleman arrived in Minnesota after 392 games in Calgary, and 22 games in he looks like the same player: fast, physical and pointed at the net. He has 6 goals and 12 points playing just under 16 minutes a night, with 40 hits, and the Wild have been winning with him in the lineup. His three-point night in Boston on Nov. 14 was his first with the club.

The goals are honest. His expected goals, the quality of his chances, sit at 6.63, almost exactly his 6. What has run hot is everything around him: teammates have finished well above their chances while he's on the ice. His shot volume has dipped too, with one or two shots most nights lately, so the scoring pace is worth watching.

The defensive side is the reason he gets trusted minutes. Evolving-Hockey rated him in the 96th percentile among forwards at taking chances away last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 87th percentile for chances from in front of the net. Two Stanley Cups in Tampa explain the rest.
headline: Blake Coleman is giving Minnesota exactly what it hoped
